mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month leads to a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to compressed credit spreads and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-rate hike period (t-test p > 0.05) during the same month, or credit spread widening is absent.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls by more than 0.2 percentage points in a month, labor market tightening is interpreted as a signal of economic resilience, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a control period with similar UNRATE changes (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production of at least 2% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as a sign of improving supply-demand balance.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO drops ≥2% in month t, then rises above INDPRO[t-1] in month t+1
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified pattern window.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month, it indicates persistent inflationary pressure, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns over the next month.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the subsequent month compared to the month before the CPI shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the monthly ratio of residential mortgage applications (PAYEMS) by at least 10% for two consecutive months signals tightening credit conditions, which predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls ≥10% in month t and again in month t+1
failure_condition: Over the 60-day window, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically worse than during a baseline period of stable mortgage applications (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of retail sales (HOUST) to prior month exceeds 1.05 for two consecutive months, it signals resilient consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified pattern window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% and a rise in manufacturing payrolls (RSAFS) by at least 2% in the same month creates a labor market tightening signal that predicts positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During the 5-day window, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) compared to a period with similar UNRATE and RSAFS movements but no simultaneous convergence.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in industrial production (INDPRO) turns positive after two consecutive months of decline, it indicates a bottoming-out in supply constraints, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO 12-mo change > 0 following two consecutive months of INDPRO 12-mo change ≤ 0
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the recovery window, or the pattern is not followed by a subsequent upturn in economic activity.
